Here is the updated spreadsheet. Start Year and End Year are derived from the Object Date column. Where a date is a single year, both columns hold that year. Where it is a range, I used the range endpoints. "ca." and "probably" are dropped, BCE dates are negative numbers (for example, -600 for 600 BCE, since "ca. 600–550 BCE" becomes -600 and -550), and blank dates are left empty.

Notes on the conventions used:
- Centuries become their full span (e.g., "18th century" → 1700–1799), and "early/mid/late" qualifiers map to sub-ranges (early = first third, mid = middle third, late = last third, roughly).
- Two rows have no date at all ("Bauhaus Archive" and "The Annunciation"), so their columns are empty.
- "ca. 1981–1550 B.C." and similar are read as -1981 to -1550; "3rd–1st century BCE" maps to -300 to -1 since there is no year zero.
